summary: Backoff retry causes signature header truncation leading to duplicate function-call side effects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when using the SDKs with exponential backoff on transient 5xx/429 errors, the X-Redwood-Signature header value is being truncated on retries after a proxy re-write. In their setup this leads to mismatched idempotency/signature tokens at the webhook receiver and results in duplicate downstream function executions.

Impact:
- Customer is on Dedicated and is observing duplicated webhook-triggered side effects (charging and order fulfillment) in production for ~0.3% of requests during light traffic spikes.
- Requires manual reconciliation by Ops; urgent due to finance impact.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated: prod/us-east-1
- SDKs in use: python 1.8.2, typescript 2.3.0, go 0.9.1
- Webhook receiver: internal order-service behind a proxy that enforces a 256-byte header length limit
- Models: llama2-13b and redwood-chat-small-v1

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Make a funcall-based request with a signed X-Redwood-Signature header and idempotency metadata attached to the session.
2) Induce transient 502 from an intermediate gateway (simulate network flapping).
3) SDK triggers exponential backoff and retries using the same logical idempotency token but the gateway truncates the signature header on retry due to header re-encoding and length limit.
4) Redwood gateway accepts retry; webhook receiver rejects truncated signature and treats the incoming retry as a new request, leading to duplicate function invocation.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate tool/function invocations at the receiver in ~0.3% of retries under simulated proxy truncation.
- Retries show identical body hashes but different X-Redwood-Signature values (one truncated).

Expected behavior:
- Retries should either carry an intact signature or the platform should surface a deterministic idempotency key mapping that is independent of header length so receivers can deduplicate safely.

Logs & artifacts provided by customer:
- Example request IDs: rq_8f9a3, rq_8f9a4
- Packet capture showing header truncated from 512b to 250b on retry path through proxy
- Minimal reproduction repo (Python) showing exponential backoff config and webhook endpoint code

Requested outcome:
- Guidance on SDK best practices and recommended header encoding to avoid truncation across proxies
- Short-term workaround to prevent duplicate side effects in customer's environment
investigation_notes:
- Support reproduced header truncation locally by inserting an nginx reverse-proxy with proxy_set_header limits and replayed the customer's backoff sequence.
- Observed: SDK retry sends same Authorization and X-Redwood-Signature header; proxy re-encodes headers and splits long headers, causing truncation.
- Gateway accepts truncated header; webhook receiver verifies signature and fails verification path, treating retry as new call.
- Root cause appears to be: (a) reliance on full-length signature header for deduping at receiver; (b) intermediaries that re-encode or clamp header lengths on retry flows.
- Confirmed cross-language: reproduced with Python and TS SDK repros; Go example provided by customer shows same pattern.
- No evidence of server-side idempotency key loss within Redwood platform; token mapping present in logs.
- Related to prior tickets about header truncation and proxy re-write (linked issues).
workaround:
Recommendations provided to customer: 1) Switch to using a compact base64url encoding of the signature in X-Redwood-Signature to keep header size < 250 bytes. 2) Mirror signature into a JSON body field with a short checksum header: e.g., X-Redwood-Sig-Chk for quick reject/dedupe at receiver. 3) Configure webhook receiver to dedupe using body-hash + idempotency token rather than raw signature. 4) Configure proxy to preserve single-line headers (nginx: proxy_set_header, proxy_buffer_size) and raise header size limits if possible.
Customer applied approach (1) and reported duplicate rate dropped to 0.01% in initial validation.

Short-term mitigation implemented by Support: added an SDK warning in Python and TS when signature exceeds 250 bytes and surface a helper to emit compact_signature().

resolution: Workaround provided and SDK helper shipped to reduce oversized signatures; customer confirmed significant reduction of duplicates. SDK patch scheduled for next minor release to include compact_signature helper and runtime warning. Follow-up: engineering task to support server-side idempotency tolerance for truncated signatures (linked ISSUE INT-21345).
next_steps:
- SDK team to land PR adding compact_signature helper (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412).
- Add a brief KB article for customers describing header size pitfalls and recommended dedupe patterns.
- Track long-term change to allow body-fingerprints as canonical dedupe key on gateway side.
- Customer to validate in production for two weeks and report metrics back to Support.
internal_notes:
- This ticket sits at the intersection of SDK ergonomics and networking edge cases. Consider adding a section to SDK best-practices for environments with legacy proxies.
- Low-frequency but high-severity because of billing/fulfillment side effects.
- Recommend adding an automated test in SDK CI that simulates header truncation and verifies helper suggestions still allow deduping.
